title: Minimum Distance Between Three Equal Elements II
summary: Given an integer array, find the minimum distance of any three identical elements.
statement: Given an integer array, find the minimum distance of any three identical elements. If no such triplet exists, return -1. The distance is calculated as the sum of absolute differences between their indices.
constraints: nums contains up to 100,000 values between one and n.
Choose three distinct indices holding the same value.
Minimize the sum of their three pairwise index distances, or return negative one if impossible.
hints: For sorted indices i<j<k, the three-distance sum simplifies to 2(k-i).
Group occurrence indices by value and inspect every consecutive triple in each group.
Minimize twice the gap between the first and third occurrence.
Any nonconsecutive triple can move an endpoint inward to a skipped equal occurrence without increasing its span, so a consecutive optimum exists.
editorial: Any nonconsecutive triple can move an endpoint inward to a skipped equal occurrence without increasing its span, so a consecutive optimum exists.

tests.explanation: Indices 0,2,3 have total pairwise distance six.
Indices 2,4,6 holding two have distance eight.
